source_text: Ὅτι δὲ καὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν γενόμενος ἄνθρωπος παθεῖν καὶ ἀτιμασθῆναι ὑπέμεινε καὶ πάλιν μετὰ δόξης παραγενήσεται, ἀκούσατε τῶν εἰρημένων εἰς τοῦτο προφητειῶν. Ἔστι δὲ ταῦτα· „Ἀνθ᾿ ὧν παρέδωκαν εἰς θάνατον τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ μετὰ τῶν ἀνόμων ἐλογίσθη, αὐτὸς ἁμαρτίας πολλῶν εἴληφε καί τοῖς ἀνόμοις ἐξιλάσεται. Ἴδε γὰρ συνήσει ὁ παῖς μου, καὶ ὑψωθήσεται καὶ δοξασθήσεται σφόδρα. Ὃν τρόπον ἐκστήσονται πολλοὶ ἐπὶ σέ, οὕτως ἀδοξήσει ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπων τὸ εἶδός σου καὶ ἡ δόξα σου ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, οὕτως θαυμάσονται ἔθνη πολλά, καὶ συνέξουσι βασιλεῖς τὸ στόμα αἰτῶν· ὅτι οἷς οὐκ ἀνηγγέλη περὶ αὐτοῦ ὄψονται, καὶ οἳ οὐκ ἀκηκόασι συνήσουσι. Κύριε, τίς ἐπίστευσε τῇ ἀκοῇ ἡμῶν; καὶ ὁ βραχίων κυρίου τίνι ἀπεκαλύφθη; Ἀνηγγείλαμεν ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ὡς παιδίον, ὡς ῥίζα ἐν γῇ διψώσῃ. Οὐκ ἔστιν εἶδος αὐτῷ οὐδὲ δέξα· καὶ εἴδομεν αὐτόν, καὶ οὐκ εἶχεν εἶδος οὐδὲ κάλλος, ἀλλὰ τὸ εἶδος αὐτοῦ ἄτιμον καὶ ἐκλεῖπον παρὰ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους. Ἄνθρωπος ἐν πληγῇ ὢν καὶ εἰδὼς φέρειν μαλακίαν, ὅτι ἀπέστραπται τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, ἠτιμάσθη καὶ οὐκ ἐλογίσθη. Οὗτος τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν φέρει καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν ὀδυνᾶται, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐλογισάμεθα αὐτὸν εἶναι ἐν πόνῳ καὶ ἐν πληγῇ καὶ ἐν κακώσει. Αὐτὸς δὲ ἐτραυματίσθη διὰ τὰς ἀνομίας ἡμῶν καὶ μεμαλάκισται διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν· παιδεία εἰρήνης ἐπ᾿ αὐτόν, τῷ μώλωπι αἰτοῦ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν. Πάντες ὡς πρόβατα ἐπλανήθημεν, ἄνθρωπος τῇ ὁδῷ αὐτοῦ ἐπλανήθη· καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν ταῖς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, καὶ αὐτὸς διὰ τὸ κεκακῶσθαι οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ. Ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείροντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος, οὕτως οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ. Ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ ἡ κρίσις αὐτοῦ ἤρθη“. Μετὰ οἶν τὸ σταυρωθῆναι αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ γνώριμοι αὐτοῦ πάντες ἀπέστησαν, ἀρνησάμενοι αὐτόν· ὕστερον δέ, ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστάντος καὶ ὀφθέντος αὐτοῖς καὶ ταῖς προφητείαις ἐντυχεῖν, ἐν αἷς πάντα ταῦτα προείρητο γενησόμενα, διδάξαντος, καὶ εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνερχόμενον ἰδόντες καὶ πιστεύσαντες καὶ δύναμιν ἐκεῖθεν αἰτοῖς πεμφθεῖσαν παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ λαβόντες καὶ εἰς πᾶν γένος ἀνθρώπων ἐλθόντες, ταῦτα ἐδίδαξαν καὶ ἀπόστολοι προσηγορεύθησαν.
pass_a_gloss: That he also became human for us and endured to suffer and be dishonored and will come again with glory, hear the prophecies spoken to this effect. There are these: 'For which he gave his soul to death and was reckoned with the lawless, he himself bore the sins of many and will make atonement for the lawless. For my servant will understand, and he will be exalted and greatly glorified. As many will be astonished at you, so your appearance will be dishonored among men and your glory among men, so many nations will marvel, and kings will shut their mouths in awe; for those who have not been told about him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.' 'Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? We announced him before him like a child, like a root in dry ground. He has no appearance or attractiveness; and we saw him, and he had no appearance or beauty, but his appearance was dishonored and lacking among men.' A man in suffering, knowing how to bear weakness, because his face was turned away, he was dishonored and not reckoned. This one bears our sins and suffers for us, and we reckoned him to be in pain and in suffering and in evil. But he was wounded for our lawlessness and bruised for our sins; a discipline of peace was upon him, by his bruise we were healed. All we like sheep have gone astray, each one on his own way has gone astray; and he gave him over to our sins, and he because of his affliction did not open his mouth. Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer he is silent, so he does not open his mouth. In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. After he was crucified and all who knew him denied him, having renounced him, but later, having risen from the dead and appeared to them and having encountered the prophecies in which all these things were spoken as going to happen, having taught, and having ascended into heaven and having seen and believed and having received power sent from there by him and having come to every nation of men, they taught these things and were called apostles.

pass_b_english: Since he also became human for our sake, endured suffering and dishonor, and will come again with glory, listen to the prophecies spoken to this effect. They are these: 'Because he gave his soul to death and was reckoned among the lawless, he himself bore the sins of many and will make atonement for the lawless. For my servant will understand, and he will be exalted and greatly glorified. Just as many will be astonished at you, so your appearance will be dishonored among men and your glory among men; so many nations will marvel, and kings will shut their mouths in awe, because those who have not been told about him will see, and those who have not heard will understand. Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? We announced him before him like a child, like a root in dry ground. He has no appearance or attractiveness; and we saw him, and he had no appearance or beauty, but his appearance was dishonored and lacking among men. A man in suffering, knowing how to bear weakness, because his face was turned away, he was dishonored and not reckoned. This one bears our sins and suffers for us, and we reckoned him to be in pain and in suffering and in evil. But he was wounded for our lawlessness and bruised for our sins; a discipline of peace was upon him, by his bruise we were healed. All we like sheep have gone astray, each one on his own way has gone astray; and he gave him over to our sins, and he because of his affliction did not open his mouth. Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer he is silent, so he does not open his mouth. In his humiliation his judgment was taken away' (Isaiah 53:3-12). After he was crucified and all who knew him deserted him, denying him, but later, having risen from the dead and appeared to them and encountered the prophecies in which all these things were spoken as going to happen, having taught, and having ascended into heaven and seen and believed and received power sent from there by him and come to every nation of men, they taught these things and were called apostles.
